name: IN-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with R+15 partisan lean
Incumbent Houchin has a massive financial advantage ($1.2M cash vs ~$18K)
Prediction markets price Democratic chances at about 4%
No public polling or expert ratings to shift the picture
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Houchin: a heavily Republican southern Indiana seat, an incumbent with a huge fundraising edge, and markets giving Meyer roughly a 4% chance. With no polls or ratings suggesting movement, the forecast stays near the baseline at about a 17-point Republican margin.
model.watch: A late surge in Democratic spending or a polling surprise showing Houchin under 55% would be the main signal this is closer than expected.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Erin Houchin, the Republican incumbent, is heavily favored to win a second full term in this southern Indiana district, which leans about 15 points Republican. Her Democratic challenger, Brad Meyer, has raised just over $100,000 and had under $20,000 on hand, while Houchin has raised $1.9 million and holds more than $1.1 million in cash. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot but is not a factor.

Prediction markets give Democrats only about a 4% chance, and no public polls or expert ratings cover the race. With the incumbent's financial dominance and the district's strong lean, the expected margin is roughly 17 points Republican, with modest uncertainty given the absence of polling.
